As shown in the figure, a curling stone enters three rectangular regions perpendicularly with speed v and undergoes uniformly decelerated motion, and just as it is about to leave the third rectangular region its speed is exactly zero. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, three left-right adjacent rectangular regions can be seen, separated by two vertical boundary lines, and the three regions have the same width; the curling stone is drawn on the far left, indicating that it enters perpendicularly from left to right and passes through the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd rectangular regions in sequence. Reasoning: Let the width of each rectangular region be L. The textual conditions of the problem give that the curling stone undergoes uniformly decelerated motion throughout the whole process, and when it has just left the 3rd rectangular region its speed is zero. Looking at the motion in reverse, it can be equivalently regarded as the curling stone starting from rest at the right boundary of the 3rd region and undergoing uniformly accelerated motion. In reverse, the distance from the endpoint to the left boundary of the 3rd region is L, to the left boundary of the 2nd region is 2L, and to the left boundary of the 1st region is 3L. From uniformly accelerated motion from rest s=(1/2)at^2, it can be known that the accumulated times to reach these positions are proportional to the square roots of the distances, so T_L:T_{2L}:T_{3L}=1:√2:√3. The times for passing through the 3rd, 2nd, and 1st regions in the forward direction respectively correspond to T_L, T_{2L}-T_L, and T_{3L}-T_{2L} in reverse. Therefore, in the forward order, the time ratio for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd regions is t_1:t_2:t_3=(T_{3L}-T_{2L}):(T_{2L}-T_L):T_L=(√3-√2):(√2-1):1.
